_comment: Camera bus registry. Generate entries with `uv run python -m hardware.bench.cameras discover` on cell1 (plug the camera in first), then fill in name + location. path MUST be a /dev/v4l/by-path entry — it encodes the physical hub port, which is what stays stable across reboots (the ELP boards all share one USB serial). solo = full-res view + interval stills; tile = the reduced profile the 3x3 view uses. still_interval_s 0 disables interval capture for that camera.
_rewired_2026_07_27: Kyle moved the cameras onto a powered hub and added a second, so BOTH paths changed — that is by-path working as designed, not a fault: identity is physical location, so re-cabling is a new identity. `cameras check` reported the old bench entry MISSING and both live cameras UNKNOWN, which is exactly the signal to re-register. Which camera was which was settled by capturing a frame from each and LOOKING, not inferred from port numbers: hub port 3.4 sees the arm from above, hub port 3.3 sees the bench from table level.

cameras.name: bench
cameras.location: MOUNTED 2026-07-28: back wall, printed 60 deg bracket, screw line 28-7/8 in above the table top centred on the arm's line (y 62.25), lens ~26.6 in up looking down the main table at the work zone. Identity confirmed by LOOKING at a frame, not inferred: it shows the table from above with the gripper at the far end and 4 tags locked.
cameras.notes: ELP-USBFHD01M-L36, 3.6mm, first camera of the fleet. Path has now changed three times by design - root port 1 direct (2026-07-25), root port 2 hub port 4 (2026-07-27), and root port 1 hub port 4 on a DIFFERENT PCI controller (05:00.4, 2026-07-28) after the cell rebuild. by-path IS the identity, so re-cabling is a new identity and the registry is expected to need updating; that is the feature, not a fault.

cameras.name: side
cameras.location: UNMOUNTED, and the NAME IS STILL PROVISIONAL - was table level looking across the bench toward the arm. It has no stand at all (717.5); target in 713.9 is ~90 deg azimuth from the arm's reach axis, ~268 mm standoff, 100-200 mm above the table
cameras.notes: Second camera, added 2026-07-27, root port 2 hub port 3. NAME AND LOCATION ARE PROVISIONAL — taken from what its first frame showed (a low view across the bench with table tags in frame), not from Kyle. Rename once he says what it is for. Worth keeping a low angle regardless: the overhead camera cannot see HEIGHT above the table and this one can, which is what a grasp approach needs.
